message.content:
The consensus among critics and audiences alike was that **“Nomadland”** (2020) was the standout film of the year. ### Why “Nomadland” tops the list | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Accolades** | • 2021 Academy Award for Best Picture (the first film shot entirely on a smartphone to win)
• Best Director (Chloé Zhao), Best Actress (Frances McDormand), Best Adapted Screenplay (Chloé Zhao & Jason Reitman) | | **Critical reception** | • Rotten Tomatoes: 94% fresh (average rating 8.2/10)
• Metacritic: 88/100 (universal acclaim) | | **Cultural impact** | • Sparked conversations about the gig economy, rural America, and the definition of “home.”
• Inspired a wave of documentaries and feature films exploring similar themes. | | **Story & performances** | • A quiet, contemplative narrative following Fern (McDormand) as she travels across the American West in her van.
• McDormand’s understated, deeply human performance earned her an Oscar and cemented her status as one of the era’s most respected actresses. | | **Technical achievements** | • Shot on a Canon EOS R5, the film showcased how high‑end smartphone cameras can produce cinematic quality.
• The cinematography by Joshua James Richards captured the vastness of the American landscape in a way that felt both intimate and epic. | ### Other strong contenders from 2020 | Film | Highlights | |------|------------| | **The Father** | • Anthony Hopkins’ Oscar‑winning performance; a masterclass in portraying dementia. | | **Minari** | • A tender, culturally rich story about a Korean‑American family; won the Grand Jury Prize at Sundance. | | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | • A timely political drama that resonated with contemporary social movements. | | **Soul** | • Pixar’s philosophical take on life and purpose; won Best Animated Feature. | ### Bottom line While opinions vary—some prefer the political punch of “The Trial of the Chicago 7” or the heartfelt storytelling of “Minari”—the overwhelming critical consensus and the sweeping awards haul make **“Nomadland”** the best movie of 2020. If you haven’t seen it yet, it’s a must‑watch for its artistry, emotional depth, and cultural relevance.
